question.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z/2}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3-z}}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$
question.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type III regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le x\le \frac{z}{2},\,\,x\le y\le z+1\}, \\ {R}_{2} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,2\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{3-z},\,\,x\le y\le z+1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/b9d4ce5d2594c8d857cbc456b1e9a098deade7f012ad6b90edc17f06b7ffde13.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le \frac{z}{2}\}\,\cup \,\{(x,z)\,:\,2\le z\le 3,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{3-z}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ is

$$
x=\frac{z}{2}\,⟹\,z=2x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
x=\sqrt{3-z}\,⟹\,z=-{x}^{2}+3.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,2x\le z\le -{x}^{2}+3\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/e89d26f7f129901b2ff004cac31c0d643c86fff5cf38ef559311131ac4122e0e.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2x}^{-{x}^{2}+3}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$
